paracetamol.use: Used for temporary relief of mild to moderate pain (e.g., headache, toothache, body ache) and to reduce fever.
warnings: Do not exceed the maximum daily dose on the label.
Avoid taking with other paracetamol-containing products (duplicate ingredient risk).
Use with caution in liver disease or regular heavy alcohol use.
Overdose can cause serious liver damage — seek urgent help even if the person feels well.

ibuprofen.use: Used for temporary relief of mild to moderate pain, inflammation and fever.
warnings: Take with or after food.
Avoid in people with stomach ulcers or GI bleeding history.
Avoid if asthma is worsened by NSAIDs/aspirin, or NSAID allergy.
Caution in kidney disease, heart disease and with anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin) or lithium.
Generally avoided in pregnancy unless advised by a doctor.

aspirin.use: Used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain and fever in adults.
warnings: Do NOT give to children or teenagers under 16 (risk of Reye's syndrome).
Increases bleeding risk; avoid with anticoagulants unless prescribed.
Avoid with stomach ulcers, NSAID allergy or NSAID-sensitive asthma.
Avoid in pregnancy unless prescribed.

naproxen.use: Used for relief of pain such as period pain and musculoskeletal pain in adults.
warnings: Take with food.
Avoid with stomach ulcers, NSAID allergy/asthma, kidney disease.
Interacts with anticoagulants and lithium.
Avoid in pregnancy unless prescribed.

cetirizine.use: Used for relief of allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, itchy/watery eyes (hay fever) and itchy skin rash (urticaria).
warnings: Low-sedating, but some people may feel drowsy — check before driving.
Avoid alcohol.
Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney disease.

loratadine.use: Used for relief of hay fever symptoms and itchy skin allergies.
warnings: Non-sedating for most people.
Check label for age limits.
Caution in severe liver disease.

fexofenadine.use: Used for relief of seasonal allergic rhinitis (hay fever) symptoms.
warnings: Non-sedating for most people.
Avoid taking with fruit juice or antacids close to the dose (reduced absorption).

chlorphenamine.use: Used for relief of allergy symptoms; causes drowsiness.
warnings: Causes drowsiness — do not drive or operate machinery.
Avoid alcohol and other sedatives.
Caution in glaucoma, prostate enlargement and in older adults (confusion, falls).

diphenhydramine.use: Used short-term for occasional sleeplessness in adults and for allergy symptoms.
warnings: Causes drowsiness; next-day drowsiness possible — do not drive.
Not recommended for older adults (confusion, falls, urinary retention).
Avoid in glaucoma and prostate enlargement.
Short-term use only; persistent insomnia needs assessment.

antacid.use: Used for temporary relief of heartburn, acidity and indigestion by neutralising stomach acid.
warnings: Separate from other medicines by about 2 hours (can reduce their absorption).
Caution in kidney disease.
Refer if symptoms persist, or with alarm signs (difficulty swallowing, weight loss, vomiting blood, black stools).

alginate.generic: Sodium alginate + Sodium bicarbonate + Calcium carbonate
alginate.use: Used for relief of heartburn and acid reflux; forms a protective layer on stomach contents.
warnings: Contains sodium — caution in salt-restricted diets.
Separate from other medicines by about 2 hours.
Persistent symptoms need medical review.

famotidine.use: Used for short-term relief of heartburn and acid indigestion by reducing stomach acid production.
warnings: Short-term self-care only; persistent symptoms need review.
Check with a doctor during pregnancy.
Dose adjustment in kidney disease.

omeprazole.use: Used for short-term relief of frequent heartburn by reducing stomach acid production.
warnings: Self-care courses are short (as per label); longer use needs medical review.
Refer alarm symptoms: difficulty swallowing, weight loss, vomiting blood, black stools, age over ~55 with new symptoms.
Check with doctor in pregnancy.

loperamide.use: Used for short-term symptomatic relief of acute diarrhoea in adults.
warnings: Do not use if there is blood in the stool or high fever — refer.
Not for children under 12 (as per most labels).
Maintain fluids; ORS is the priority in dehydration.
Stop and seek advice if no improvement within 48 hours.

ors.use: Used to replace fluids and electrolytes lost through diarrhoea or vomiting.
warnings: Mix with the exact volume of clean water stated on the pack.
Discard prepared solution as directed on the label (commonly after 24 hours).
Seek medical help for signs of severe dehydration, blood in stool, or in young infants.

zinc.use: Used alongside ORS in children with diarrhoea, as recommended in WHO guidance.
warnings: Use the dose on the label for the child's age.
May cause nausea.

simethicone.use: Used to relieve trapped wind, gas and bloating.
warnings: Persistent abdominal pain needs medical assessment.
Infant colic that is severe or with fever, vomiting or poor feeding needs a doctor.

lactulose.use: Used for relief of constipation; draws water into the bowel to soften stools.
warnings: May take 1–2 days to work.
May cause wind and cramps initially.
Refer if constipation persists, or with blood in stool, weight loss or severe pain.

ispaghula.use: Used to relieve constipation by increasing stool bulk.
warnings: Take with plenty of water; do not take immediately before bed.
Not for bowel obstruction or difficulty swallowing.

bisacodyl.use: Used for short-term relief of occasional constipation in adults.
warnings: Short-term use only.
May cause abdominal cramps.
Do not take within 1 hour of antacids or milk.

senna.use: Used for short-term relief of occasional constipation.
warnings: Short-term use only; usually works in 8–12 hours.
May colour urine.
Refer if no improvement or alarm symptoms.

dextromethorphan.use: Used for temporary relief of a dry, tickly (non-productive) cough.
warnings: Not for chesty/productive cough.
Do not use with MAO inhibitors or within 14 days of stopping them.
May cause drowsiness or dizziness.
Misuse potential at high doses.
Refer a cough lasting more than about 3 weeks.

guaifenesin.use: Used to help loosen mucus in a chesty (productive) cough.
warnings: Drink plenty of fluids.
Refer if phlegm is green/bloody with fever, breathlessness or chest pain, or cough > ~3 weeks.

linctus.use: Used to soothe a dry, irritated throat and tickly cough.
warnings: Contains sugars (honey) — not suitable for diabetics without advice.
Honey-containing products are not given to infants under 1 year.

lozenge.use: Used to soothe a sore throat; mild antiseptic action.
warnings: Not for children under 6.
Refer if sore throat lasts more than a week, or with difficulty swallowing/breathing or high fever.

benzydamine.use: Used for temporary relief of painful sore throat and mouth inflammation.
warnings: May cause numbness or stinging.
Refer persistent symptoms.

saline.use: Used to moisten nasal passages and help clear a blocked or dry nose.
warnings: Generally suitable for most ages including infants (drops).
Do not share nasal devices.

xylometazoline.use: Used for short-term relief of nasal congestion.
warnings: Do not use for more than 7 days (risk of rebound congestion).
Caution in high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma.
Use the paediatric strength only as per age on label.

pseudoephedrine.use: Used for short-term relief of nasal and sinus congestion in adults.
warnings: Avoid in high blood pressure, heart disease, overactive thyroid, glaucoma.
Do not use with MAO inhibitors.
May cause insomnia and restlessness.
Sale is restricted in many countries.

coldCombo.use: Used for temporary relief of multiple cold symptoms (fever, aches, congestion, runny nose).
warnings: Contains paracetamol — do not take with other paracetamol products.
Contains a decongestant — avoid in high blood pressure/heart disease or with MAO inhibitors.
Contains a sedating antihistamine — may cause drowsiness.
Regulators have questioned the effectiveness of oral phenylephrine as a decongestant.
Avoid in pregnancy unless advised by a doctor.
